**Summary**

I researched Apple's results on the web and decided to buy, then placed a single order within your mandate. Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 results (period ended September 28, 2024, reported October 31) showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and the FY2024 Form 10-K reported total net sales of $391.035 billion (up from $383.285 billion), operating income of $123.216 billion, net income of $93.736 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (down slightly from $6.13, in a year that included a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge) — a picture of solid top-line growth with stable-to-slightly-lower reported earnings, which I read as a healthy enough backdrop to add to the name. I ignored several low-quality "MarketWatchers" roundup links and quarantined snippets rather than relying on unverifiable numbers. With AAPL trading at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought 44 shares at a limit of $222.90 — a limit essentially at the ask, ~0.1% above the last price — for roughly $9,808 (~$9,799 notional), leaving you with $50,000 cash previously on hand minus this outlay, and a total of just this one $10k-class order today, well within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with no money moved out of the account. The order filled at $222.90.
